identity.title: The uncertain interstellar medium of high-redshift quiescent galaxies: Impact of methodology

paper_type_evidence.quote: We obtained the raw data from the ALMA Science Archive and processed them to produce calibrated visibility sets, which were then split and binned in both time and channels, and finally exported as a single continuum UVFITS table per QG with GILDAS[^1].

In this Letter, we revisited the REQUIEM-ALMA literature sample of six lensed QGs. We analyzed the ALMA Band 6 continuum observations of these galaxies, described in W21, with a different methodology and assumptions.

question.value: Whether the apparent tension between low dust/gas fractions derived from resolved observations of strongly lensed quiescent galaxies (W21) and higher fractions derived from stacked FIR SEDs (G18, M21) is an artifact of methodology and assumptions.

evidence.quote: It is therefore not immediately clear whether the apparent tension between these two types of constraints is not simply an artifact of mismatched assumptions.
To remedy this doubt, we revisited the lensed QG sample of W21 using a methodology consistent with that of G18 and M21.

The REQUIEM-ALMA sample (W21) consists of six QGs at $z=1.5-3.2$ observed under programs 2018.1.00276 (PI K.E. Whitaker) and 2019.1.00227 (PI J. Tan) with the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 1.3 mm, corresponding to the ALMA Band 6 and $300-500$ $\mu$m rest frame.

evidence.quote: However, we caution that, while at least one object (MRG-2129) has 0.13% dust, implying $f_{\text{gas}}\sim10$%, the upper limits derived here remain compatible with much lower ISM fractions, which makes it difficult to draw firm conclusions on quenching scenarios from these data.

findings_qualitative.value: Both the FIR flux extraction method (point source vs. extended stellar model) and the light-to-mass conversion factor (S16 vs. M21 SED) strongly impact derived dust fractions, combining to produce up to an order of magnitude variation.

evidence.quote: We found that, while some tension with SED-derived results might still exist, the method used for FIR flux extraction and the light-to-mass conversion factor both have a significant impact on the estimate of their dust fractions, with both adding up to an order of magnitude variation.

findings_qualitative.value: Using extended stellar light models and the M21 SED makes the Md/M* constraints of the REQUIEM-ALMA sample broadly consistent with the 0.08-0.09% values derived from FIR stacks of unlensed QGs.

evidence.quote: Under our physically motivated assumptions, the constraints on the dust fraction of this sample are broadly consistent with the $M_d/M_{\star}\sim0.08-0.09$% values derived by G18 and M21 for coeval QGs from lower-resolution FIR stacks.

findings_qualitative.value: MRG-0138 remains almost an order of magnitude more dust-poor than the other five QGs even under the extended model and M21 SED analysis, which may reflect an anticorrelation between ISM fraction and stellar mass.

evidence.quote: The notable exception is MRG-0138 which, even in this new analysis, remains almost an order of magnitude more dust-poor than the other five QGs.

Its tension with the stacked results of G18 and M21 might then be explained by an anticorrelation between ISM mass and stellar mass being already present at this epoch, which would be largely diluted with them being averaged over large samples with relatively broad stellar mass ranges.

claims.hypothesis: The apparent tension between low dust/gas mass fractions inferred from resolved ALMA observations of lensed QGs (W21) and higher values from stacked FIR SEDs (G18, M21) is largely caused by differences in flux extraction methodology and dust temperature/SED assumptions.
claims.experiment: Re-extracted 1.3 mm continuum fluxes in the uv-plane using HST F160W extended stellar light models (plus optional central point sources) and converted fluxes to dust masses using the lower-temperature (Td = 21 K) QG FIR SED from M21.
claims.result: Using the M21 SED raises Md/M* by a factor of 3-3.5 over the S16 calibration, and using the extended emission model raises Md/M* by another 25%-50% for detections and a factor of 3-5 for upper limits.
claims.finding: The combined methodology choices account for up to an order of magnitude variation in Md/M*, relaxing or eliminating the tension with stacked FIR SED constraints for five of the six galaxies.

evidence.quote: The first case yields the lowest $M_d/M_{\star}$, while the second one produces values higher by a factor $3-3.5$.
Using the extended emission model (third case) raises $M_d/M_{\star}$ by another 25%-50% for detected objects and a factor 3-5 in the case of upper limits, depending on the size of the galaxy.
In particular, opting for extended models based on the stellar surface brightness of the targets has the effect of relaxing, if not eliminating, said tension.

claims.hypothesis: The 1.3 mm dust emission in the detected lensed QGs (MRG-2129 and MRG-0138) can be described by an extended component following the stellar light distribution rather than solely compact central emission.
claims.experiment: Fitted the ALMA Band 6 uv visibilities with the HST F160W stellar light model alone and with an additional central point source, comparing residuals against a pure point-source model.
claims.result: MRG-2129 is well-fitted by the extended stellar light model alone (yielding 247 +/- 66 uJy, 50% larger Md than compact-only), whereas MRG-0138 requires an additional compact component accounting for ~45% of the total flux per image (total 352 +/- 116 uJy).
claims.finding: Extended dust emission following the stellar distribution is viable and increases the recovered flux, though MRG-0138 still requires a central compact component and current data depth cannot definitively distinguish the true dust geometry.

evidence.quote: Of the two point-like detections in W21, the emission of MRG-2129 is well-fitted by the extended stellar light model (Fig. [1](#fig:cutouts), right) without compact emission, with slightly lower residuals than when using a point source; although, the difference is not significant.
On the other hand, MRG-0138 requires an additional point-like component, accounting for $\sim$45% of the total flux per image.

claims.hypothesis: MRG-0138 is genuinely dust-poor compared to typical high-z QGs in FIR stacks even when analyzed with an extended source model and a cold QG SED.
claims.experiment: Computed Md/M* for MRG-0138 using the extended F160W model + point source flux (352 +/- 116 uJy), the M21 SED conversion, and recomputed stellar mass (log(mu M*) = 13.05).
claims.result: MRG-0138 remains almost an order of magnitude more dust-poor than the other five QGs in the sample and well below the Md/M* ~ 0.08-0.09% stacked average.
claims.finding: The scant dust content of MRG-0138 is confirmed and is likely due to its extreme stellar mass, early quenching at z >= 3, and subsequent dust destruction over time.

evidence.quote: The notable exception is MRG-0138 which, even in this new analysis, remains almost an order of magnitude more dust-poor than the other five QGs.
On the other hand, we confirm the scant dust content of MRG-0138 determined in W21.

why_this_data.value: The REQUIEM-ALMA sample of six strongly lensed QGs was previously used by W21 to infer very low dust/gas fractions in tension with FIR SED stacks, making it the direct benchmark needed to test whether methodology drives the discrepancy.

evidence.quote: To remedy this doubt, we revisited the lensed QG sample of W21 using a methodology consistent with that of G18 and M21.

why_this_method.value: Using HST F160W stellar light models for uv-plane flux extraction reproduces the effective aperture of low-resolution FIR SED stacks (minus neighbor contamination), and the M21 FIR SED template (Td = 21 K) reflects the softer radiation field expected in quiescent galaxies.

evidence.quote: The use of these stellar light models should therefore come closest to reproducing the effective aperture of the SED stacks in M21, minus the potential residual contamination by nearby sources.

In addition to being consistent with the methodology of M21, with which we compare in this study, we consider it a more likely description of the ISM of QGs which, given their quiescence, should be subjected to a softer radiation field than in SF galaxies.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Extended model fit combined with the Scoville et al. (2016) star-forming calibration was omitted for clarity because it falls between the other three tested combinations and can be easily inferred from them.

evidence.quote: For clarity, we do not include the fourth possible combination here, that is, the extended model fit with the S16 calibration, as it falls between the first and third method and can be easily inferred from the first three (see Sect. [\[results\]](#results)).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Separating the two lensed images of MRG-0138 bisected by a critical line was rejected in favor of modeling them as a single combined image with two point-source components of fixed relative amplitude.

evidence.quote: One exception was MRG-0138, where the lensed arc targeted by the ALMA observation is a combination of two images bisected by a critical line. We did not attempt to separate them, but rather counted them as a single image, thus requiring the use of two point-source components, with relative amplitudes fixed by the ratio of mean magnifications between the two images given in N18.

limitations_admitted.value: Zeroing out pixels below 3 sigma in the F160W cutouts to avoid image noise might cut out some of the galaxies' extended stellar profiles.

evidence.quote: We note that, while this threshold was chosen to avoid including image noise in the model, it might cut out some of the galaxies’ extended profiles.

limitations_admitted.value: If dust and stars do not have comparable distributions in the source plane, differential lensing magnification across images would affect Md/M* and require a full lensing model.

evidence.quote: We note that, in any other case, correctly estimating $M_d/M_{\star}$ would require the usage of a full lensing model to account for differential magnification across images.

limitations_admitted.value: Four of the six galaxies remain undetected at 3 sigma, leaving upper limits that are compatible with much lower ISM fractions and preventing firm conclusions on quenching scenarios.

evidence.quote: However, we caution that, while at least one object (MRG-2129) has 0.13% dust, implying $f_{\text{gas}}\sim10$%, the upper limits derived here remain compatible with much lower ISM fractions, which makes it difficult to draw firm conclusions on quenching scenarios from these data.

limitations_admitted.value: VLT/MUSE spectra only cover the rest-frame near-ultraviolet, which is suboptimal for reconstructing star formation histories and insensitive to completely dust-shrouded stellar populations.

evidence.quote: However, we caution that, although the absorption features covered by the MUSE spectra correlate with a combination of age and metallicity (cite: Fan92; Mar09), being limited to the near-ultraviolet, which is most sensitive to young massive stars, makes them suboptimal for reconstituting SFHs. In addition, some stellar populations could be invisible if, for example, they are entirely shrouded by dust.

referee_caveats_inferred: The preference for the extended stellar model over a point-source model in MRG-2129 is not statistically significant in the residuals, meaning the higher flux and dust mass depend on an unverified prior that dust follows the optical stellar light.
